hero.headline: Trump pardons former GOP congressman convicted of insider trading
hero.body:
President Donald Trump issued a full pardon for Steve Buyer, a former Indiana Republican congressman who was convicted of insider trading in 2023. The pardon clears Buyer of federal criminal charges related to securities violations.

Buyer, who served in the House of Representatives, was found guilty of using confidential information to trade stocks. The conviction came after a federal investigation into his financial transactions during his time in Congress and afterward. Federal prosecutors had argued that Buyer exploited insider knowledge for personal financial gain.

The pardon represents one of Trump's most recent uses of executive clemency power. Presidential pardons are final and cannot be overturned by courts or other government branches. They restore civil rights and remove the legal consequences of federal convictions.

Trump has previously used the pardon power for political allies and supporters. The decision to pardon Buyer has drawn attention given the nature of the conviction and Buyer's past role as a Republican member of Congress. Former Vice President Pence recently stated that Jan. 6 rioters who assaulted police or vandalized property should not receive pardons from Trump, highlighting ongoing debates about the appropriate use of presidential clemency.

Buyer's pardon comes as Trump faces political headwinds heading into midterm elections, with approval ratings at new lows and growing tensions with Senate Republicans. The pardon power remains one of the president's most absolute constitutional authorities, requiring no approval from Congress or the courts.

cards.headline: US and Iran exchange fire as ceasefire frays in Gulf
cards.body:
The United States and Iran traded military strikes on Thursday in the most serious test yet of their month-long ceasefire. The exchange involved US forces intercepting Iranian drones headed toward Bahrain and Kuwait, followed by American retaliatory strikes on Iranian radar installations.

Iran accused Washington of breaching the truce by targeting two ships in the Strait of Hormuz and attacking civilian areas. The US military maintained it had struck in response to the Iranian drone launches. Both sides blamed each other for initiating the latest round of hostilities.

Hours after the initial exchange, Bahrain reported that Iran had fired ballistic missiles and drones at it and Kuwait. Air raid sirens sounded in Bahrain, with residents instructed to move to safe locations. Kuwait's military said it was intercepting both drones and missiles launched at the country.

President Donald Trump told reporters in Washington DC that the ceasefire remained intact despite the strikes. When asked about prospects for a negotiated end to the conflict, Trump was noncommittal, saying a deal "might not happen, but it could happen any day." He expressed confidence that Iran wanted a settlement more than he did.

Before the strikes, reports suggested the two sides were nearing an agreement to halt the war. A one-page memorandum had been shared between Washington and Tehran via Pakistan, indicating possible progress in negotiations. However, the latest military clashes have further stalled talks, with neither side showing significant movement toward a lasting resolution.

The incidents test the durability of the ceasefire arrangement that both nations previously agreed to honor. Military officials from each country have offered conflicting accounts of responsibility for breaking the agreement, with each side insisting the other initiated the violence.

Adding to tensions, the Treasury Department is preparing to make Iranian frozen assets available to US partners in the region for reconstruction purposes. A source familiar with the matter said the US plans to use these assets to help Gulf allies recover from damage caused by Iran. This move is likely to further inflame relations between Washington and Tehran.

The latest flare-up comes as the broader conflict continues to have ripple effects globally. Japan has begun experiencing shortages of plastic bags and food service materials due to disruptions in naphtha supplies from the Middle East, where Iran's war has impacted oil production. Meanwhile, the US labor market showed resilience with 172,000 jobs added in May, though stock markets experienced significant sell-offs amid uncertainty from the ongoing Middle East crisis.

The fragile ceasefire now faces its greatest challenge as both sides accuse each other of violations and show little willingness to return to meaningful peace negotiations.

cards.headline: US plans to redirect Iranian assets to Gulf allies for repairs
cards.teaser: The Treasury Department is preparing to make frozen Iranian funds available to help US partners in the Gulf recover from damage.
cards.body:
The United States is planning to use frozen Iranian assets to fund reconstruction efforts in Gulf allied nations, according to a source familiar with the plans. The Treasury Department intends to make Iranian funds available to help US partners in the region repair damage caused by Iran.

The move comes as tensions between Washington and Tehran remain high following recent military exchanges in the Gulf. Making Iranian assets available to countries affected by Iranian actions could further strain relations between the two nations as peace talks continue to stall.

cards.headline: US Debt Sustainability Analysis Points to Crisis Risk
cards.teaser: Researchers have estimated the maximum sustainable debt level before interest payments could trigger an economic crisis.
cards.body:
New analysis from budget forecasters examines when federal debt reaches unsustainable levels, with projections suggesting the United States could hit the debt ceiling again as soon as late winter. The Penn Wharton Budget Model and other researchers have attempted to quantify how much debt the country can carry before interest payments become unmanageable.

The research comes as the federal government faces mounting borrowing costs and competing budget priorities. Forecasters predict the US will approach a 41 trillion dollar debt ceiling in the coming months. The analysis focuses on the point at which debt service costs could spark a fiscal crisis, forcing difficult choices about government spending and revenue. Interest payments on the national debt continue growing as a share of the federal budget.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Discusses Government Stake in AI Companies
cards.teaser: The White House is exploring a plan to give the federal government equity positions in major artificial intelligence firms.
cards.body:
President Trump said his administration would explore taking ownership stakes in leading AI companies, describing the prospect as "a beautiful thing." The administration plans to meet with AI companies next week to discuss arrangements where American taxpayers could benefit from AI industry success.

The discussions include exploring potential government equity structures with OpenAI and other major AI firms. Trump framed the proposal as a way for the American people to share in the gains from artificial intelligence development.

cards.headline: Multiple people shot near festival in Toledo, Ohio
cards.body:
Multiple people have been shot near the Old West End Festival in Toledo, Ohio, with authorities still searching for suspects, according to the Toledo Police Department.

The shooting took place Saturday afternoon near the festival, a community event typically held in the neighborhood. Police and medical personnel responded to the scene in large numbers following the incident.

"Many victims" have been taken for medical treatment, the Toledo Police Department said in a statement. The department is actively investigating the shooting and has asked the public to avoid the area while the search for suspects continues.

The Old West End Festival is an annual gathering in Toledo that usually serves as a family-oriented community event. The shooting disrupted what is typically a peaceful celebration in the neighborhood.

Authorities have not yet disclosed the total number of people injured or specific details about the condition of the victims. The investigation is ongoing as law enforcement works to identify and locate those responsible for the attack.

Police have urged anyone with information about the incident to contact the Toledo Police Department as the investigation develops.

cards.headline: Federal Reserve Governor Warns of Risks from Easing Bank Regulations
cards.body:
Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr has warned that regulatory relief measures for large banks have primarily benefited shareholders rather than borrowers, raising concerns about financial stability as the industry enters a period of deregulation.

Barr cautioned that loosening rules on major financial institutions during a period of economic strength could introduce vulnerabilities to the banking system. His comments come as policymakers continue to debate the appropriate level of oversight for large financial institutions.

The regulatory relief measures implemented in recent years were designed to reduce compliance costs and encourage banks to increase lending to businesses and consumers. However, Barr's analysis suggests that banks have used the profits gained from deregulation primarily to reward shareholders rather than expand lending activity. This outcome contradicts the original intent of the relief measures.

Barr's primary concern focuses on the timing of deregulation during what he described as a financial boom period. When markets are performing well and bank profits are strong, reducing regulatory requirements may leave the banking system exposed to significant risks when economic conditions change. He argued that regulatory standards should be designed to account for cyclical economic risks and maintain safeguards even during periods of apparent stability.

The debate over banking regulation has intensified as financial institutions have reported strong earnings while questions persist about whether looser rules compromise the overall safety of the financial system. Barr's position represents a more cautious approach within the Federal Reserve, emphasizing the need to balance industry concerns about regulatory burden against the critical importance of preventing financial crises.

His warnings come against the backdrop of previous banking sector turmoil that required government intervention to prevent broader economic damage. The current regulatory trends, according to Barr's analysis, may be moving too far in favor of industry preferences at the potential expense of systemic stability. This creates a tension between different regulators and political leaders who must weigh competing priorities for financial oversight.

The discussion also reflects broader questions about the relationship between banking regulation and economic outcomes. While deregulation advocates argue that reducing compliance costs helps banks operate more efficiently, Barr's concerns highlight the potential dangers of reducing protections during economically favorable conditions. His position suggests that regulators should maintain stronger safeguards during booms to prevent excessive risk-taking that could threaten stability during downturns.

As policymakers continue to debate the appropriate regulatory framework for the financial system, Barr's public warnings signal that disagreement exists within the Federal Reserve about how aggressively to pursue deregulation. His emphasis on maintaining adequate safeguards during periods of economic strength suggests that future policy debates over banking regulation will remain contested among senior officials responsible for managing financial stability.

cards.headline: Ukraine launches drone strikes on St. Petersburg
cards.teaser: Ukrainian forces targeted military facilities in Russia's second-largest city in what Moscow called an unprecedented attack.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones struck St. Petersburg on Saturday, targeting military facilities and oil infrastructure in Russia's second-largest city. The attack came hours after President Vladimir Putin attended an economic forum there. Russian authorities urged residents to stay indoors—a first since the war began.

This marked the second drone strike on St. Petersburg in recent days, reflecting Ukraine's expanding long-range attack capabilities. Russia described the assault as unprecedented.

cards.headline: Israeli attack kills Lebanese general and two soldiers
cards.teaser: The Israeli military said it is investigating an incident in south Lebanon where three Lebanese soldiers died.
cards.body:
A Lebanese general and two soldiers were killed in an Israeli attack on their car in south Lebanon on Saturday. The incident occurred in an area where Israeli forces are conducting operations against Hezbollah.

The Israeli military said it is investigating the attack. The deaths represent a significant escalation in the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah in the region.

cards.headline: Israeli fire kills infant in West Bank, Palestinian officials say
cards.teaser: Palestinian officials reported a baby was killed after an Israeli soldier opened fire on a vehicle.
cards.body:
An infant was killed when Israeli military forces fired on a car in the West Bank, according to Palestinian officials. The Israeli military said a soldier opened fire after troops perceived a vehicle accelerating toward them. The baby's grandmother, who was in the car, disputed that account.

The incident adds to ongoing tensions in the occupied West Bank, where Israeli forces maintain a significant military presence. The conflicting accounts from Israeli and Palestinian sources highlight the deep divisions over events in the territory.

cards.headline: Iran says staff denied US visas for World Cup despite player clearance
cards.teaser: Iranian officials say technical staff have been blocked from entering the United States hours after players received visa approval.
cards.body:
A diplomatic dispute has erupted over US visa approvals for Iran's World Cup delegation just days before the tournament begins. On June 5, the United States approved visas for Iran's players and some staff members to compete in the competition, where the team will play all three group-stage matches in the US.

However, Iranian state media and officials reported that same day that several support staff members were denied entry, including Iranian football federation chief Mehdi Taj. The team departed for Mexico on June 6 to begin preparations, with players granted access but key technical personnel blocked from entering the country.

cards.headline: US defense secretary criticizes Europe on migration during Normandy speech
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth used a D-Day anniversary event to attack European migration policies.
cards.body:
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth criticized European migration policies during a speech in Normandy marking 82 years since the Allied D-Day landings in 1944. He used beach invasion imagery when discussing migration, drawing attention for the unconventional focus during the historical commemoration event.

The speech occurred as officials gathered to remember the operation that liberated Nazi-occupied northwestern Europe during World War II.

cards.headline: Federal prosecutors launch election probe in California
cards.teaser: The U.S. attorney's office in California has announced an investigation into elections as millions of ballots remain uncounted.
cards.body:
The U.S. Department of Justice sent a federal prosecutor to observe ballot processing in Los Angeles as California's gubernatorial primary continued with millions of ballots still being counted. The delayed results prompted the federal monitoring effort.

The slow ballot count has drawn scrutiny, including baseless claims of election fraud from national figures. California state officials have rejected these allegations, but the delay in results has fueled misinformation about the integrity of the elections.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth criticizes European migration policy in Normandy speech
cards.teaser: U.S. Defense Secretary Hegseth attacked Europe over migration in a speech at Normandy, 82 years after D-Day.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Hegseth delivered remarks in Normandy criticizing European migration policy, describing it as a beach invasion. He was speaking at the site where allied forces launched their operation to liberate Nazi-occupied northwestern Europe 82 years ago.

The speech marked the anniversary of the D-Day landings in 1944, with Hegseth using the historic setting to draw comparisons between the World War II operation and current European migration patterns.

cards.headline: Israeli attack kills Lebanese general and two soldiers in south Lebanon
cards.teaser: Three Lebanese soldiers, including a general, were killed in an Israeli attack on a car in southern Lebanon.
cards.body:
A Lebanese general and two other soldiers were killed when Israel attacked their car in south Lebanon. The Israeli military is investigating the incident, which occurred in an area where Israeli forces are fighting Hezbollah.

The attack targeted a vehicle carrying Lebanese military personnel in southern Lebanon. Israel has been conducting operations against Hezbollah in the region, and the Israeli military has opened an investigation into the strike that killed the Lebanese soldiers.

cards.headline: Social media fuels skincare obsession among young girls
cards.teaser: Experts warn about long-term impacts as girls fall into a skincare consumption pattern some are calling cosmeticorexia.
cards.body:
Social media is driving a boom in the children's skincare market, with young girls increasingly drawn into elaborate skincare routines and products. The trend has created a growing market segment as cosmetics companies target this younger demographic with skincare content online.

Experts are concerned about the long-term impact on girls' development and wellbeing, particularly the psychological effects of encouraging children to focus on skincare and beauty products at young ages.

cards.headline: Police officer joins Love Island cast, faces criticism in hometown
cards.teaser: Sean Reifel joined the reality show less than a year after becoming a police officer, drawing backlash from his community.
cards.body:
Sean Reifel joined the cast of Love Island US less than a year after becoming a police officer in his hometown. His decision to appear on the reality dating series has drawn backlash from residents who question whether the role is appropriate for someone serving in local law enforcement.

The controversy reflects broader concerns about how police officers present themselves publicly and the image they project to their communities.

cards.headline: Gamers campaign to keep games playable after publishers shut down servers
cards.teaser: Stop Killing Games is challenging the practice of publishers shutting down games without ensuring they remain accessible.
cards.body:
A group called Stop Killing Games is challenging publishers' practice of shutting down games without ensuring they remain playable. The campaign questions whether companies should be able to make purchased games inaccessible by discontinuing server support.

The movement argues that players should retain the ability to play games they've bought, even after official support ends. Stop Killing Games is pushing back against the industry standard that allows publishers to render games permanently unplayable without providing alternatives or transferring functionality to players.

cards.teaser: The White House is exploring a plan to give the federal government equity positions in major artificial intelligence firms.
cards.body:
President Trump said his administration would explore taking ownership stakes in leading AI companies, describing the prospect as "a beautiful thing." The administration plans to meet with AI companies next week to discuss arrangements where American taxpayers could benefit from AI industry success.

The discussions include exploring potential government equity structures with OpenAI and other major AI firms. Trump framed the proposal as a way for the American people to share in the gains from artificial intelligence development.

cards.headline: Florida Sues OpenAI Over ChatGPT Safety Concerns
cards.teaser: The state filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman alleging the company marketed ChatGPT despite serious user safety risks.
cards.body:
Florida filed a lawsuit claiming OpenAI allowed its ChatGPT system to aid and abet mass shooters, raising allegations about the company's responsibility for harmful uses of its technology. The complaint accuses the AI company of marketing its chatbot while aware of serious risks to user safety.

The case represents what some observers are calling a potential Big Tobacco moment for the artificial intelligence industry, as state attorneys general begin pursuing legal theories of liability for AI harms. Florida Republicans have ramped up regulatory action on AI under Governor Ron DeSantis. The lawsuit marks an escalating legal challenge for OpenAI as it faces questions about how its systems can be misused and what obligations the company has to prevent harmful applications.

cards.headline: Chip Sector Selloff Erases Over One Trillion Dollars in Market Value
cards.teaser: Semiconductor stocks fell sharply, with Micron dropping 13 percent and the broader chip industry losing more than a trillion dollars.
cards.body:
Micron stock plunged 13 percent, contributing to a massive selloff across the semiconductor sector that wiped out 1.3 trillion dollars in market value. Major chipmakers including Nvidia, Broadcom, and Micron all experienced significant declines as investors questioned whether the rally in chip stocks had peaked early.

Analysts described the decline as a crack in Wall Street's hottest trade, with the semiconductor industry having driven substantial market gains in recent months. The sharp reversal raised questions about whether investors should buy the dip or whether the selloff signals deeper concerns about chip demand and valuation. The losses reflect shifting sentiment about artificial intelligence infrastructure spending and semiconductor supply dynamics.

cards.headline: Eli Lilly Reports Positive Data for Next Generation Obesity Drug
cards.teaser: The pharmaceutical company's triple agonist retatrutide showed improvements in weight loss, diabetes control, and related health conditions.
cards.body:
Eli Lilly's experimental drug retatrutide, a triple agonist, demonstrated substantial improvements across multiple health metrics in clinical studies. The medication reduced weight and hemoglobin A1C levels while also improving knee osteoarthritis pain and obstructive sleep apnea symptoms.

The results position retatrutide as a potential advance in obesity treatment, capable of addressing multiple complications simultaneously rather than weight alone. Lilly is positioning the drug as part of a new generation of weight management therapies.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Remain Stable Despite Major Supply Disruption
cards.teaser: Crude oil has not reached extreme price levels even after what analysts describe as the biggest supply shock in history.
cards.body:
Oil prices have stayed well below 200 dollars per barrel despite experiencing what market observers characterize as the largest supply shock in the industry's history. The relative price stability has surprised analysts who expected more extreme market reactions to the disruption.

Several factors may explain the muted price response, including increased production from other sources, changes in global demand patterns, and strategic reserve releases. The situation demonstrates how oil markets have evolved, with greater flexibility and alternative supply options moderating the impact of individual supply shocks compared to previous decades.

hero.headline: Chemists demonstrate how RNA may have copied itself on early Earth
hero.body:
Chemists have demonstrated for the first time how RNA could have replicated itself on early Earth, potentially solving a long-standing puzzle in origin-of-life research. The breakthrough addresses a fundamental question that has challenged scientists for decades: how the first genetic material could have reproduced without the complex cellular machinery that exists today.

The research shows a mechanism by which RNA molecules could have copied themselves in conditions similar to those believed to have existed on the primitive Earth. RNA is considered a crucial molecule in the emergence of life because it can both store genetic information like DNA and catalyze chemical reactions like proteins. This dual functionality has led many scientists to propose that an "RNA world" preceded the DNA-based life forms that exist today.

The self-replication of RNA has been a bottleneck in origin-of-life studies because modern cells use elaborate protein machinery to copy genetic material. Understanding how this process could have occurred without that machinery has been a major challenge. The demonstration provides experimental evidence for a pathway that could have allowed early RNA molecules to reproduce themselves without requiring the presence of evolved biological systems.

The work represents a significant advance in understanding how life could have emerged from non-living chemistry. By showing a plausible mechanism for RNA self-replication under early Earth conditions, the research helps fill a critical gap in theories about how the first living systems developed. The findings support the RNA world hypothesis, which proposes that self-replicating RNA molecules were a key stepping stone in the transition from chemistry to biology.

The demonstration offers a concrete answer to one of the most fundamental questions in science: how life began. While many steps in the origin of life remain uncertain, this research provides experimental backing for a process that must have occurred if RNA-based life preceded modern cellular organisms.

cards.headline: OpenAI introduces Lockdown Mode to defend against prompt injection attacks
cards.teaser: The new security feature aims to protect sensitive data from malicious prompts, though vulnerabilities may remain.
cards.body:
OpenAI has launched Lockdown Mode, a security feature designed to protect ChatGPT from prompt injection attacks. These attacks attempt to manipulate AI systems by embedding malicious instructions within user inputs to expose sensitive data or trigger unintended actions.

The new feature aims to reduce the likelihood that sensitive information will be shared during such attacks. OpenAI acknowledges that ChatGPT could still remain vulnerable to prompt injections even with Lockdown Mode enabled, but the goal is to minimize potential data exposure when these attacks occur.

cards.headline: Scientists removed from diabetes conference after distributing journal reprints
cards.teaser: Those ejected included the editor-in-chief of an ADA journal and a former ADA president.
cards.body:
Multiple scientists were ejected from an American Diabetes Association conference for distributing reprints of journal articles. Among those removed were Steven Kahn, editor-in-chief of an ADA journal, and Desmond Schatz, a former president of the organization.

The incident highlighted tension within the diabetes research community, as the ADA took action against prominent figures within its own ranks for their activities at the conference.

cards.headline: Trump administration explores taking equity stake in OpenAI
cards.teaser: President Trump said he is discussing arrangements that would allow the American people to benefit from AI success.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump said his administration is considering deals that would give the government an equity position in OpenAI. According to Trump, these arrangements would allow "the American people to benefit from the success of AI."

The discussions represent a potential shift in how the federal government engages with artificial intelligence companies, moving from regulatory oversight to direct financial participation in the sector's growth.

cards.headline: Sriram Krishnan departs role as White House AI advisor
cards.teaser: Krishnan is reportedly launching a new institution to continue influencing Trump administration AI policy.
cards.body:
Sriram Krishnan has left his position as AI advisor in the White House. Krishnan had been serving in the Trump administration, providing guidance on artificial intelligence policy and strategy.

According to reports, Krishnan plans to start a new institution that will continue to shape the administration's approach to AI policy. The move suggests he intends to maintain influence over federal AI decision-making from outside the government structure.

cards.headline: Predictive surrogates could reduce quantum computing measurement overhead by over 99 percent
cards.teaser: Researchers report a technique that could dramatically cut the resources needed for quantum measurements.
cards.body:
A new approach using predictive surrogates could reduce the measurement overhead in quantum computing by more than 99.97 percent, according to research published in a physics journal. Measurement overhead refers to the computational resources required to extract useful information from quantum systems.

The technique addresses a significant challenge in practical quantum computing, where measuring quantum states requires substantial resources. By cutting overhead so dramatically, the approach could make quantum computers more efficient and expand their practical applications.

cards.headline: Fossils reveal largest scorpion ever reached over three feet in length
cards.teaser: The ancient creature had six-inch pincers and lived 415 million years ago, according to new research.
cards.body:
Fossils from 415 million years ago have uncovered the largest scorpion species on record, measuring over three feet long with six-inch pincers. These giant arthropods inhabited both land and water environments in what is now the United Kingdom during the Devonian Period.

The prehistoric scorpions were roughly the size of baseball bats, dwarfing all scorpion species alive today. This discovery provides striking new insights into the scale of ancient arthropods.

hero.headline: Golden Tempo wins Belmont Stakes after Kentucky Derby victory
hero.body:
Golden Tempo won the 158th running of the Belmont Stakes, extending an earlier victory at the Kentucky Derby. The horse crossed the finish line at Saratoga Race Course in a nine-horse field that competed under rainy conditions.

The Belmont Stakes is one of thoroughbred racing's three Triple Crown events. Golden Tempo's success at both the Kentucky Derby and Belmont Stakes represents a significant achievement in horse racing. However, the horse did not compete in the Preakness Stakes, the middle leg of the Triple Crown series.

Weather conditions affected the race at Saratoga Race Course, where rain created slower track conditions throughout the competition. These circumstances influenced the pace and performance of all entries in the field. The win adds to Golden Tempo's strong showing in major stakes races this season.

The 158th edition of the Belmont Stakes featured multiple Grade 1 stakes races throughout the day at the upstate New York track. The Belmont Stakes has been held at different venues throughout its history. This year's running took place at Saratoga rather than at its traditional Belmont Park location.

Golden Tempo's victories in two of racing's most prestigious events represent a major accomplishment for the horse's ownership and training team. The Kentucky Derby and Belmont Stakes wins establish the horse among the year's top thoroughbred racing competitors, despite not attempting a full Triple Crown sweep.

The Triple Crown has been called the most difficult feat in American sports, requiring a horse to win three prestigious races held at different distances in different states over a five-week span. Only 13 horses have swept all three events since Sir Barton accomplished the feat in 1919. The most recent Triple Crown winner was Justify in 2018.

An increasing number of Derby winners have recently skipped the Preakness because of the short turnaround between the two races. Industry discussions have explored moving the Preakness to three weeks after the Derby rather than its current two-week timing, a change aimed at encouraging top horses to compete in all three Triple Crown races.

The racing landscape continues to shift as Churchill Downs Inc recently acquired intellectual property rights to the Preakness Stakes and the Black-Eyed Susan Stakes from 1/ST Maryland LLC. The acquisition brings the Preakness under the same corporate ownership as the Kentucky Derby. Churchill Downs said the transaction is expected to close after the 2026 running of the Preakness.

Meanwhile, media rights for the Preakness are in flux. NBC's broadcasting contract expires after this year's running. Multiple bidders including NBC, Fox, Amazon and Netflix have expressed interest in acquiring the next rights deal, underscoring the event's continued value in the sports landscape.

cards.headline: US men's soccer team falls to Germany 2-1 in final World Cup warmup
cards.teaser: Germany defeated the United States 2-1 in Chicago as both teams completed their final preparation match before the World Cup.
cards.body:
The United States men's national team lost 2-1 to Germany in their final World Cup warmup match at Soldier Field in Chicago. Antonee Robinson scored the Americans' only goal in front of a sellout crowd of 63,636 fans.

The loss concluded US preparations before the tournament begins. The team will open World Cup play on June 12 against Paraguay.

cards.headline: Scotland defeats Bolivia 4-0 in World Cup warmup match
cards.teaser: Scotland scored four first-half goals in a dominant victory over Bolivia in their final preparation match before the World Cup.
cards.body:
Scotland beat Bolivia 4-0 in their final World Cup warm-up match, with all four goals scored in the first half. It was the first meeting between the two nations. Manager Steve Clarke's side will face Haiti in their World Cup opener next weekend.

The dominant performance provided Scotland with significant momentum ahead of their first World Cup appearance in 28 years. A clinical display of finishing and buildup play dispelled concerns about their opening group match, offering genuine hope that Scotland could progress from the group stage for the first time in their international history.

cards.headline: Knicks take 2-0 lead over Spurs in NBA Finals
cards.teaser: The New York Knicks won Game 2 of the NBA Finals to take a two-game series lead over the San Antonio Spurs.
cards.body:
The Knicks defeated the Spurs in Game 2 to move ahead 2-0 in the NBA Finals series. The game featured close plays and key decisions in the final moments that went in favor of the Knicks, helping secure the victory.

Despite the series advantage, the Knicks stated the job is far from complete. The Spurs have not conceded the series, with Game 3 scheduled to take place in New York with increased security measures expected.

cards.headline: Michael van Gerwen beats Luke Humphries to win Nordic Darts Masters
cards.teaser: Michael van Gerwen came from behind to defeat Luke Humphries 8-7 in the final leg of the Nordic Darts Masters in Denmark.
cards.body:
Michael van Gerwen claimed the Nordic Darts Masters title in Denmark with a dramatic 8-7 victory over Luke Humphries. The Dutchman came from behind to win in the final leg, securing his place at the top of the tournament.

The thrilling finish added another significant title to van Gerwen's professional darts career.

cards.headline: Chris Billam-Smith stops Ryan Rozicki in Zuffa Boxing UK debut
cards.teaser: British boxer Chris Billam-Smith defeated Ryan Rozicki by technical knockout after seven rounds in Bournemouth.
cards.body:
Britain's Chris Billam-Smith delivered a gritty performance to mark Zuffa Boxing's UK debut, stopping Ryan Rozicki by technical knockout after seven gruelling rounds in Bournemouth. 

The victory highlighted Billam-Smith's endurance through the intense clash, cementing the significance of the event as Zuffa Boxing's first show in the British market.

cards.headline: Denny Hamlin takes pole position for NASCAR race at Michigan
cards.teaser: Denny Hamlin earned the Busch Light pole position for Sunday's NASCAR race at Michigan International Speedway.
cards.body:
Hamlin secured the top starting position in qualifying at Michigan, giving him the lead spot for the green flag. Chase Elliott will lead Hendrick Motorsports cars in the race starting on Sunday.

The qualifying results set the field for the weekend's race at Michigan International Speedway. Multiple drivers from Hendrick Motorsports will start near the front of the pack.

hero.headline: Anthony Head, Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Ted Lasso actor, dies at 72
hero.body:
Anthony Head, the British actor best known for playing Rupert Giles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, has died at age 72. He passed away peacefully from complications related to pneumonia, surrounded by his family, according to a statement from his daughters Emily and Daisy Head.

"It has been, and forever will be, an honour and a privilege to be his daughters, and to have witnessed first-hand the impact both he and his work have had on so many," they said.

Head played Giles, the school librarian and mentor to Sarah Michelle Gellar's title character, throughout Buffy the Vampire Slayer's seven-season run from 1997 to 2003. The role established him as a beloved figure in television and introduced him to audiences worldwide. Sarah Michelle Gellar paid tribute to Head on Instagram, beginning with a quote from her Buffy character: "Tell Giles I figured it out and I'm ok." She then wrote, "Well I don't have it figured out and I'm not ok. But I know I'm the lucky one because I knew you."

Beyond Buffy, Head's career spanned decades in British and American television, theater, and film. He had a recurring role in the BBC sketch show Little Britain and appeared in the BBC production of Merlin. His film credits included The Iron Lady and The Inbetweeners Movie. More recently, he played former football club owner Rupert Mannion in the Emmy-winning Apple TV+ series Ted Lasso, where he developed strong on-screen chemistry with co-creator Jason Sudeikis.

Born in Camden, London, Head came from an artistic family. His father founded Verity Films as a documentary filmmaker, while his mother was an actress who appeared in the 1960s BBC crime drama Maigret. His brother also pursued acting.

Head began his professional career on stage, starring in the 1978 West End revival of Godspell. He later took roles in films including the 1981 adaptation of Lady Chatterley's Lover and 1987's A Prayer for the Dying. In the early 1980s, he sang backing vocals for British pop group Red Box and appeared on their 1986 debut album.

He was perhaps best known in the United Kingdom and United States for his role in Nescafe Gold Blend television advertisements during the 1980s. The stage remained central to his career, with notable roles including Freddie Trumper in the original West End production of the Abba musical Chess in 1988, and Dr. Frank-N-Furter in the 1990 West End production of The Rocky Horror Show.

During Buffy's production, Head commuted between Los Angeles and England, where his partner and two young daughters lived. "I'd try to go home to them every three or four weeks," he told the Guardian, noting that the production team accommodated his schedule.

His daughters stated that Head "loved his job very much and he always considered himself incredibly lucky to have been able to work alongside such exceptionally talented people, in such wonderful productions, across a career that spanned several decades."

cards.headline: Florida police close investigation into Hulk Hogan's death
cards.teaser: Clearwater police released their final report on the death of wrestling icon Hulk Hogan, ruling it natural and closing their investigation.
cards.body:
Florida police shared their final report on the death of Hulk Hogan, the professional wrestling legend who died in 2025. The Clearwater Police Department concluded their investigation and ruled the death natural.

The release of the files comes after Hogan's daughter Brooke Hogan raised questions about the circumstances surrounding her father's death. The Clearwater police issued a statement confirming the conclusion of their investigation and the release of related documents.

cards.headline: Patrick Godfrey, Ever After actor, dies at 93
cards.teaser: Patrick Godfrey, the English actor who played Leonardo da Vinci in the 1998 film Ever After: A Cinderella Story, died at age 93.
cards.body:
Patrick Godfrey, the English actor best known for portraying Leonardo da Vinci in the 1998 fantasy film "Ever After: A Cinderella Story," has died at age 93. His death was announced on Thursday by his talent agency, Markham Froggatt Irwin.

Godfrey had a long career in film and television, with his role in the Cinderella adaptation among his most notable performances.

cards.headline: Scott Pelley thanks supporters after 60 Minutes firing
cards.teaser: Former 60 Minutes correspondent Scott Pelley thanked fans for their support after the show's new executive producer fired him.
cards.body:
Scott Pelley posted on Instagram to thank supporters following his firing from 60 Minutes. The veteran correspondent was dismissed by the program's new executive producer, Nick Bilton, after a clash with management.

In his statement, Pelley accused CBS executives of instructing him to "inject falsehoods and bias" into his reporting. He emphasized that 60 Minutes' decades-long success stemmed from its commitment to "integrity, quality, and humanity," suggesting the network's new direction undermines those principles. The firing has drawn criticism from journalists and the family of late correspondent Morley Safer, who spent 46 years at the program.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo premieres new song with Robert Smith at Primavera Sound
cards.teaser: Olivia Rodrigo revealed she has a duet with The Cure's Robert Smith on her upcoming album by bringing him onstage at the Primavera Sound festival.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo surprised fans at the Primavera Sound festival by bringing The Cure's Robert Smith onstage to perform their duet "What's Wrong With Me." The collaboration appears on Rodrigo's forthcoming album, which releases in less than a week.

The reveal came as Rodrigo brought Smith out partway through her festival set. The duet between the pop star and the legendary rock musician had been kept secret until the performance.

cards.headline: Robert De Niro, Martin Scorsese reunite for Taxi Driver 50th anniversary
cards.teaser: The cast and creative team behind Taxi Driver gathered at the Tribeca Festival to mark the film's 50th anniversary.
cards.body:
Robert De Niro, Martin Scorsese, Jodie Foster, and screenwriter Paul Schrader reunited at the 2026 Tribeca Festival to celebrate Taxi Driver's 50th anniversary. During the event, De Niro performed the film's iconic "You talkin' to me?" line while the group discussed the film's creation and lasting cultural impact.

The conversation explored whether Bruce Springsteen inspired one of the film's most memorable lines. The panelists reflected on how the 1976 film's themes of isolation and obsession continue to resonate with audiences today, suggesting that these human experiences remain as relevant now as they were five decades ago.

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen cancels Pittsburgh concert due to severe weather
cards.teaser: Morgan Wallen canceled his scheduled performance at Acrisure Stadium due to severe weather conditions in the Pittsburgh area.
cards.body:
Morgan Wallen canceled his concert at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh due to severe weather conditions. This marks the second time the artist has called off a show in the city.

In response to the cancellation, a local baseball team offered free admission to fans holding tickets from the canceled concert.

hero.headline: Trump pardons former GOP congressman convicted of insider trading
hero.body:
President Donald Trump issued a full pardon for Steve Buyer, a former Indiana Republican congressman who was convicted of insider trading in 2023. The pardon clears Buyer of federal criminal charges related to securities violations.

Buyer, who served in the House of Representatives, was found guilty of using confidential information to trade stocks. The conviction came after a federal investigation into his financial transactions during his time in Congress and afterward. Federal prosecutors had argued that Buyer exploited insider knowledge for personal financial gain.

The pardon represents one of Trump's most recent uses of executive clemency power. Presidential pardons are final and cannot be overturned by courts or other government branches. They restore civil rights and remove the legal consequences of federal convictions.

Trump has previously used the pardon power for political allies and supporters. The decision to pardon Buyer has drawn attention given the nature of the conviction and Buyer's past role as a Republican member of Congress. Former Vice President Pence recently stated that Jan. 6 rioters who assaulted police or vandalized property should not receive pardons from Trump, highlighting ongoing debates about the appropriate use of presidential clemency.

Buyer's pardon comes as Trump faces political headwinds heading into midterm elections, with approval ratings at new lows and growing tensions with Senate Republicans. The pardon power remains one of the president's most absolute constitutional authorities, requiring no approval from Congress or the courts.

cards.headline: U.S. attorney's office opens election fraud investigation in California
cards.teaser: The Los Angeles U.S. attorney's office announced an investigation into potential election fraud in California's elections.
cards.body:
The U.S. Justice Department sent a federal prosecutor to Los Angeles to observe ballot processing in California's primary elections. The move came as counting continued at a slower pace than expected in races for governor, mayor and Congress.

The deployment followed repeated claims from President Trump that California Democrats were "rigging" election results. State officials have rejected the allegations as baseless. Experts cautioned that ballot-counting could extend significantly as results trickle in from multiple primary contests across the state.

cards.headline: Pence says violent Jan. 6 rioters should not receive Trump pardons
cards.teaser: Former Vice President Pence said Jan. 6 rioters who assaulted police or vandalized property should not be pardoned by President Trump.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Pence said that Jan. 6 rioters who assaulted police officers, vandalized government property or sought to disrupt certification of the 2020 presidential election should not be pardoned by President Trump and should never get a dime. He made the comments in an interview on HBO's Real Time.

The statement comes as Trump faces political pressure heading into midterm elections. Trump's approval ratings have hit new lows and tensions with Senate Republicans have spilled into public view.

cards.headline: Trump to appear on Meet the Press amid political headwinds
cards.teaser: President Trump is scheduled for an interview on NBC's Meet the Press following a week of declining approval ratings and Republican tensions.
cards.body:
President Trump is sitting down for an interview on NBC's Meet the Press following a week marked by new lows in his approval ratings and growing tensions with Senate Republicans that have spilled into public view. As midterm elections approach, the president has faced mounting political pressure on key issues including the economy.

The interview comes as Trump navigates growing friction within his own party. Republican senators have publicly expressed concerns about the administration's direction as voters prepare to head to the polls in the midterm elections.

cards.headline: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland wins New Mexico gubernatorial primary
cards.teaser: Deb Haaland, who served in the Biden administration, secured the Democratic nomination for New Mexico governor.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland won the New Mexico primary for governor. Haaland previously served as a Biden administration official and could make history as the first female Native American governor if elected in the general election.

The primary victory positions Haaland for the November general election. Her candidacy represents a potential milestone in Native American political representation at the state executive level.

cards.headline: McCarthy echoes Trump claims on California vote counting
cards.teaser: Former Speaker Kevin McCarthy criticized California's vote-counting process, supporting claims made by President Trump.
cards.body:
Former Speaker Kevin McCarthy criticized California's vote-counting process, joining President Trump and other conservatives in questioning the state's election administration. McCarthy told radio hosts that California voters were losing confidence as results continued trickling in from primary elections.

Election experts say California's gradual counting process is designed to protect against fraud and ensure every vote is counted accurately. The system includes multiple verification steps and allows voters to correct errors, which accounts for the slower pace that has drawn criticism from Trump and others.

cards.headline: California gubernatorial primary results still coming in
cards.teaser: Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer and Xavier Becerra and Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton are vying for nominations to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra are leading in California's gubernatorial primary. Democrats Katie Porter and Tom Steyer are also competing for their party's nomination, while Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton are vying for the Republican spot. Under California's primary system, the top two vote-getters will advance to the general election, regardless of party affiliation.

Vote counting continues as the state processes ballots from the primary. The winners will move forward to face off in the general election to determine who will replace Gov. Gavin Newsom.
